# varunayan

> Python package to download and process climate reanalysis and observational data. It has a focus on India, but it supports global datasets. An R package with the same functions and output is at https://varunayan.saketlab.org/R/.

varunayan gets data from ERA5 reanalysis, IMD gridded observations, HadEX3 climate extremes indices and CRU TS monthly climate grids. It also has heat stress indices (UTCI, WBGT, Heat Index, Humidex), country-level temperature, analysis and plot functions, ERA5 variable search, spatial aggregation and a download cache.

## Data Sources

- ERA5: global reanalysis from ECMWF/Copernicus CDS. 0.25 degree grid, hourly, 1940 to present. Single-level and pressure-level datasets. Regions: bounding box, point or GeoJSON polygon.
- IMD: India Meteorological Department gridded data. Rainfall at 0.25 degree (NetCDF), temperature (tmax, tmin, tmean) at 1 degree (binary .grd), 1901 to present.
- HadEX3: Hadley Centre global ETCCDI climate extremes indices. 1.25 x 1.875 degree grid, 1901 to 2018. Annual and monthly frequencies.
- CRU TS v4.07: Climatic Research Unit monthly climate grids. 0.5 degree, 1901 to 2022, land only. Variables: tmp, tmx, tmn, dtr, pre, wet, frs, vap, cld, pet.

## Installation

```
pip install varunayan
```

Requires Python 3.10+. ERA5 downloads need a CDS API key. Set CDS_API_KEY (or CDSAPI_KEY), write ~/.cdsapirc, or enter the key when varunayan asks for it.

## Modules and API

### ERA5 (`varunayan.core`)

```python
from varunayan import era5ify_bbox, era5ify_point, era5ify_geojson, spatial_mean

df = era5ify_bbox(request_id="demo", variables=["2m_temperature"], start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0, frequency="daily")
df = era5ify_point(request_id="point", variables=["2m_temperature"], start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", lat=28.6, lon=77.2)
df = era5ify_geojson(request_id="geo", variables=["2m_temperature"], start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", json_file="region.geojson", level="feature")

# Regional mean, weighted by cos(latitude)
daily = spatial_mean(df, "value", by=["variable", "datetime"])
```

Output: a long DataFrame with columns `datetime`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `pressure_level` (pressure-level data only), `variable` (ERA5 short name, for example `t2m`, `tp`) and `value`. Monthly data also has `year` and `month`; yearly data has `year`. With `convert_units=True` (default), temperatures are in Celsius and precipitation is in mm. Accumulated variables are totals for monthly and yearly data.

`era5ify_point` returns the grid cell nearest to (lat, lon). `era5ify_geojson(level="union")` (default) returns each grid cell inside the union of the features; `level="feature"` returns one row for each feature, with the mean of its cells and the feature properties in place of latitude and longitude.

Common parameters: `dataset_type` ("single" or "pressure"), `pressure_levels` (list of strings, for example ["1000", "850"]), `frequency` ("hourly", "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "yearly"; default "hourly"), `resolution` (degrees, default 0.25; not for era5ify_point), `verbosity` (0, 1, 2), `save_raw` (default False), `convert_units` (default True).

Files: each request writes `{request_id}_output/{request_id}_{frequency}_data.csv` (the long table) and `{request_id}_unique_latlongs.csv`, plus `{request_id}_raw_data.csv` when save_raw=True.

### Analysis (`varunayan.analysis`)

All functions take a long DataFrame and return a small DataFrame (or Series).

```python
from varunayan import load_india_boundaries, spatial_mean, compare, cross_correlation, anomaly, seasonal_cycle, peak_month, seasonal_stat, regrid, dewpoint_from_relative_humidity

states = load_india_boundaries("state")                       # or "district"; cached GeoDataFrame
monthly = spatial_mean(df, "value", by=["year", "month"])      # adds a date column
stats = compare(merged, x="imd", y="era5", by="state_name")    # n, r, bias, rmse
ccf = cross_correlation(x_series, y_series, max_lag=12)
monthly["anomaly"] = anomaly(monthly, "value", baseline=(1991, 2020))
cycle = seasonal_cycle(df, "value")                            # mean for each calendar month
peak = peak_month(df, "value")                                 # peak_month, peak_value, annual_total
jjas = seasonal_stat(df, "value", months=[6, 7, 8, 9], how="sum")
coarse = regrid(df, "value", resolution=1.0, by=["year", "month"])
```

### Plots (`varunayan.plot`)

Each function returns a matplotlib Figure.

```python
from varunayan import plot_map, plot_series, plot_dual_axis, plot_ccf, plot_scatter, plot_bars, plot_heatmap

plot_map(peak, "peak_month", months=True, boundaries=states)
plot_series(monthly, x="date", y="anomaly", smooth="linear")   # smooth: "lowess", "linear" or None
plot_dual_axis(merged, x="date", left="value", right="searches")
plot_ccf(ccf)
plot_scatter(merged, x="imd", y="era5")
plot_bars(stats, x="state_name", y="bias", horizontal=True, sort=True)
plot_heatmap(table, x="month", y="year", value="value")
```

### ERA5 Variable Search (`varunayan.search_and_desc`)

```python
from varunayan import search_variable, list_available_variables, describe_variables, list_variable_categories, get_variable_info, get_variable_units, get_variable_long_name, get_available_pressure_levels

search_variable("temperature")
list_available_variables(dataset_type="single")
list_variable_categories(dataset_type="single")
describe_variables(["2m_temperature", "total_precipitation"], dataset_type="single")
get_variable_info("2m_temperature")
get_variable_units("2m_temperature")
get_variable_long_name("2m_temperature")
get_available_pressure_levels()
```

### ERA5 Convenience (`varunayan.convenience`)

Wrappers that download ERA5 data and return one column for each variable.

```python
from varunayan import get_era5_daily_temperature, get_era5_daily_humidity, get_era5_daily_wind, get_era5_daily_heat_index_data, get_era5_monthly_heat_index_data, get_era5_daily_heat_index_geojson, get_era5_daily_heat_index_point

df = get_era5_daily_temperature(request_id="t", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = get_era5_daily_humidity(request_id="h", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = get_era5_daily_wind(request_id="w", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = get_era5_daily_heat_index_data(request_id="hi", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = get_era5_daily_heat_index_point(request_id="hp", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", latitude=28.6, longitude=77.2)
df = get_era5_daily_heat_index_geojson(request_id="hg", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", geojson_file="region.geojson", level="union")
```

### IMD (`varunayan.imd`)

```python
from varunayan import (
    download_imd_rainfall, download_imd_temperature,
    read_imd_rainfall, read_imd_temperature,
    imd_rainfall_bbox, imd_rainfall_geojson,
    imd_temperature_bbox, imd_temperature_geojson,
    process_imd_files, filter_imd_by_bbox, filter_imd_by_geojson,
    aggregate_imd_by_frequency,
    list_imd_datasets, get_imd_grid_specs,
)

# Download raw files
download_imd_rainfall(start_year=2020, end_year=2023)
download_imd_temperature(start_year=2020, end_year=2023, var_type="tmax")

# Read downloaded files
df = read_imd_rainfall(file_path="path.nc", resolution=0.25, year=2020)
df = read_imd_temperature(file_path="path.grd", var_type="tmax", year=2020)

# Download, read and crop in one call
df = imd_rainfall_bbox(request_id="r", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0, frequency="monthly")
df = imd_temperature_bbox(request_id="t", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0, var_type="tmax")
df = imd_rainfall_geojson(request_id="rg", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, geojson_file="region.geojson")
df = imd_temperature_geojson(request_id="tg", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, geojson_file="region.geojson", var_type="tmax")

# Post-processing
df = filter_imd_by_bbox(data=df, north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = aggregate_imd_by_frequency(data=df, frequency="monthly")

# Metadata
list_imd_datasets()
get_imd_grid_specs("rainfall_0.25")
```

IMD temperature `var_type` options: "tmax", "tmin", "tmean".

### IMD Stations (`varunayan.imd_stations`)

```python
from varunayan import get_imd_stations

stations = get_imd_stations(with_coordinates=True, max_workers=8)
```

Returns a DataFrame of IMD observation stations, with latitude and longitude when with_coordinates=True.

### HadEX3 (`varunayan.hadex3`)

```python
from varunayan import hadex3_bbox, hadex3_geojson, list_hadex3_indices

indices = list_hadex3_indices(frequency="all")
df = hadex3_bbox(index="TXx", start_year=2000, end_year=2018, north=35, south=8, east=90, west=68)
df = hadex3_geojson(index="TXx", start_year=2000, end_year=2018, geojson_file="india.geojson")
```

Annual ETCCDI indices: TXx, TXn, TNx, TNn, TX90p, TX10p, TN90p, TN10p, TR, SU, FD, ID, CSDI, WSDI, DTR, GSL, ETR, CDD, CWD, PRCPTOT, R10mm, R20mm, Rx1day, Rx5day, R95p, R99p, R95pTOT, R99pTOT, SDII. Some indices also have monthly data (`frequency="monthly"`).

### CRU TS (`varunayan.cru_ts`)

```python
from varunayan import cru_ts_bbox, cru_ts_geojson, list_cru_ts_variables

variables = list_cru_ts_variables()
df = cru_ts_bbox(variable="tmp", start_year=2000, end_year=2020, north=35, south=8, east=90, west=68)
df = cru_ts_geojson(variable="tmp", start_year=2000, end_year=2020, geojson_file="india.geojson")
```

Variables: tmp (mean temperature), tmx (maximum temperature), tmn (minimum temperature), dtr (diurnal temperature range), pre (precipitation), wet (wet days), frs (frost days), vap (vapour pressure), cld (cloud cover), pet (potential evapotranspiration).

### Country-Level Temperature (`varunayan.country`)

```python
from varunayan import get_era5_country_temperature

df = get_era5_country_temperature(country="India", start_date="2023-01-01", end_date="2023-12-31", variables=["mean", "max", "min"])
```

`country` is a name or a GeoDataFrame. `variables` is "mean", "max", "min", an ERA5 variable name, or a list. The function uses Natural Earth boundaries and cos(latitude) weights. It works for all countries. It returns year, month and one column for each variable.

### Heat Stress Indices (`varunayan.heat_stress`)

```python
from varunayan import (
    utci, utci_sparse, utci_category,
    wbgt_simple, wbgt_shade, wbgt_outdoor, wbgt_risk_category,
    heat_index, heat_index_from_dewpoint, heat_index_risk_category,
    humidex, mean_radiant_temperature,
    wet_bulb_temperature, wet_bulb_from_dewpoint,
    relative_humidity_from_dewpoint, dewpoint_from_relative_humidity,
    vapor_pressure_from_dewpoint, calc_heat_indices,
)

# UTCI (Brode polynomial). tmrt defaults to temp_c (shade).
utci_val = utci(temp_c=35.0, wind_speed=2.0, dewpoint_c=25.0, tmrt=50.0)
category = utci_category(utci_val)

# UTCI sparse Legendre polynomial (Roman et al. 2025, wider wind range)
utci_val = utci_sparse(temp_c=35.0, tmrt=50.0, wind_speed=2.0, rh=60.0)

# WBGT
wbgt_val = wbgt_simple(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
wbgt_val = wbgt_shade(temp_c=35.0, wet_bulb_c=28.0)
wbgt_val = wbgt_outdoor(temp_c=35.0, wet_bulb_c=28.0, globe_temp_c=45.0)
category = wbgt_risk_category(wbgt_val)

# Heat Index (NWS Rothfusz regression, Celsius input)
hi_val = heat_index(temp_c=35.0, rh=60.0)
hi_val = heat_index_from_dewpoint(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
category = heat_index_risk_category(hi_val)

# Humidex (ECCC)
hx_val = humidex(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)

# Mean radiant temperature
tr = mean_radiant_temperature(temp_c=30.0, solar_radiation=800.0, wind_speed=1.0)

# Wet bulb temperature and humidity helpers
tw = wet_bulb_temperature(temp_c=35.0, rh=60.0)
tw = wet_bulb_from_dewpoint(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
rh = relative_humidity_from_dewpoint(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
td = dewpoint_from_relative_humidity(temp_c=35.0, rh=60.0)
vp = vapor_pressure_from_dewpoint(dewpoint_c=25.0)

# All main indices at once: DataFrame with temp_c, dewpoint_c, rh, wet_bulb, heat_index, wbgt, humidex
results = calc_heat_indices(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
```

All functions accept floats, numpy arrays or pandas Series. Units: temperature in Celsius, wind in m/s, humidity in %, radiation in W/m2.

### Spatial Aggregation (`varunayan.spatial`)

```python
from varunayan import aggregate_to_polygons, check_grid_coverage, visualize_grid_overlap, compare_grids, get_polygon_timeseries

# Aggregate grid values to polygons, for each group in by
result = aggregate_to_polygons(data=df, polygons=gdf, value_cols="value", by=["year", "month"], fill_empty=True)

# Check how well a grid covers the polygons
coverage = check_grid_coverage(grid_data=df, polygons=gdf)

# Time series for each polygon
ts = get_polygon_timeseries(data=df, polygons=gdf, value_col="value", time_col="datetime")

# Compare grids (for example ERA5 and IMD)
compare_grids(grids={"era5": df1, "imd": df2}, polygons=gdf)
visualize_grid_overlap(grid_data=df, polygons=gdf)
```

### Processing Utilities (`varunayan.processing`)

```python
from varunayan import categorize_variables, get_aggregation_method, is_sum_var, is_max_var, is_min_var, is_rate_var

method = get_aggregation_method("total_precipitation")  # "sum"
categorize_variables(["2m_temperature", "total_precipitation"])
```

These functions give the temporal aggregation method of each ERA5 variable (sum, max, min, rate or mean).

### Cache (`varunayan.cache`)

```python
from varunayan import get_cache_dir, show_cache_info, list_cache, cache_stats, clear_cache, cache_exists, get_cached_data, save_to_cache, invalidate_cache

get_cache_dir()
show_cache_info()
df = list_cache(source="all")
stats = cache_stats()
clear_cache(source="all", older_than_days=30, confirm=False)
key = dict(request_id="demo", variables=["2m_temperature"], start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", frequency="daily")
exists = cache_exists(**key)
data = get_cached_data(**key)
save_to_cache(df, **key)
invalidate_cache(cache_key="abc123")
```

### CLI

The CLI gets ERA5 data with three subcommands: `geojson`, `bbox` and `point`.

```
varunayan bbox --request-id demo --variables 2m_temperature --start 2023-06-01 --end 2023-06-30 --north 28.7 --south 28.5 --east 77.3 --west 77.0
varunayan point --request-id pt --variables 2m_temperature --start 2023-06-01 --end 2023-06-01 --lat 28.6 --lon 77.2
varunayan geojson --request-id geo --variables 2m_temperature --start 2023-06-01 --end 2023-06-30 --geojson region.geojson --level feature
```

Common flags: `--dataset-type` (single|pressure), `--pressure-levels` (comma-separated), `--freq` (hourly|daily|weekly|monthly|yearly), `--res` (grid resolution in degrees), `--verbosity` (0|1|2), `--save-raw` (True|False; default False). GeoJSON flag: `--level` (union|feature).

IMD, HadEX3 and CRU TS do not have CLI subcommands. Use the Python API.
